# Evaluation on 40 held-out synthetic people (set b: E41-E80)

**Synthetic data, not validated with real people.** Generated by `python scripts/eval.py --write` on 2026-11-17 at commit `225f6cd`. Every number below is computed by the script; none is typed by hand. Rules: [eval/LABELING.md](../eval/LABELING.md). People: [eval/personas.json](../eval/personas.json). Labels: [eval/labels.json](../eval/labels.json), sha256 `67fc77fe212a6e9b…`, written by an independent annotator that saw only the stories, before any of these people was run through the app.

Each share: value (count/people; 95% Wilson interval). With 40 people an interval is about ±15 points wide, so small differences between versions are not evidence of anything.

How the versions were run: the same 40 profiles through each version's own API. `641f749` ran from a temporary git worktree. v1 knew 25 IT roles only and could read only education, skill levels and tools (its interest questions and IT-area preferences have no counterpart in these profiles), so most of its gap is coverage, not a better algorithm. v1 has no idea of a person's status, so its "job-search courses for people in work" are counted by the same rule.

## Why first moves concentrate (found after the first run; nothing was changed because of it)

For each of the 32 people whose first move is not in their acceptable list, the first move is compared with the best-placed acceptable occupation in their top 50 (moderate adoption). Mean points the first move is ahead by, per part of the match score:

| Part (weight) | Mean lead | First move ahead in |
|---|---|---|
| field (20%) | +0.1 | 6 of 32 |
| interest (15%) | -0.3 | 15 of 32 |
| skill (30%) | -0.2 | 13 of 32 |
| outlook (35%) | +3.6 | 25 of 32 |

- Malaysian demand, which is most of the outlook, has 15 distinct values over 910 occupations; 105 occupations share the top value 90.6 (on the MyCOL list, in the MASCO major group whose share of job ads grew most).
- 186 occupations count as on the MyCOL list, through 58 MyCOL titles: MyCOL lists MASCO unit groups, and an occupation counts when its checked ISCO-08 unit group is on the list (data/mycol_links.csv shows the ESCO match behind each link).
- 27 occupations still map to ISCO major group 2 (professionals) while O*NET's job zone is 3 or less, for example: Coroners → 2619 Legal professionals not elsewhere classified; Tax Preparers → 2411 Accountants; Telecommunications Engineering Specialists → 2153 Telecommunications engineers; Network and Computer Systems Administrators → 2523 Computer network professionals. The stage 7 check (data/isco_review.csv) corrected 9 such codes from ESCO evidence and found none for these 27: they are marked unverified, get no mapping points and count only as "near" MyCOL.
- Any further fix has to be tested on new synthetic people, not on the people it was found on.

## Limits

- The people and their labels are synthetic. One annotator (an AI agent) wrote the labels; no second annotator checked them, so label noise is unmeasured.
- Agreement means "a counsellor would accept this", not "this person would succeed in it".
- Interest answers are made from each person's three liked types by one fixed rule (`scripts/eval_personas.py`), not answered by people.
- Stage 7 (ISCO-08 check, data/isco_review.csv) changed the data under every version called "Now". On the demo people it removed the one first move that changed between slow and fast adoption (judge_check: 1 of 5 -> 0 of 5); the demo guard in tests/test_scenarios.py now asks for 2 people whose top 3 changes, not 3. Nothing was tuned.
- Phase 1 KPI 1 (career clarity of 20+ real testers) cannot be measured this way: see [impact_verification.md](impact_verification.md) and the pilot plan in the README.
